ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ (١)).
We mentioned at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara that the origin of «نَاس» according to Sībawayh is «أُنَاس», its fāʾ [the first radical] having been dropped; according to others nothing was dropped from it, and its origin is «نَوْس», because they say in the diminutive «نُوَيْس».
Some said: its origin is «نَيْس», transposed from «نَسِيَ», taking it from «النِّسْيَان» (forgetting); but this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ (٤) الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ (٥)).
(الْوَسْوَاسِ) with a fatḥa is a noun, and with a kasra it is the maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is: «مِنْ شَرِّ ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ» (from the evil of the one who whispers). It is also said that Satan was named by the act itself, for intensification. (الْخَنَّاسِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of it. (الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ) may be nominative, accusative or genitive.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ): it is a badal (substitute) for «شَرِّ» with repetition of the governor (ʿāmil), i.e. «مِنْ شَرِّ الْجِنَّةِ» (from the evil of the jinn). It is also said that it is a badal for «ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ», because the whisperer is of the jinn.
It is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُوَسْوِسُ», i.e. he whispers while being of the jinn.
It is also said that it is a badal for «النَّاسِ», i.e. in the breasts of the jinn;
and [the one who held this] made «مِنَ» explicative (tabyīn), and applied the name «النَّاس» to the jinn because they move about in pursuit of their aims.
«الْجِنّ» and «الْجِنَّة» have one meaning. It is also said that (مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ) is a ḥāl from «النَّاسِ», i.e. being of the two kinds. As for the last (النَّاسِ), it is said that it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ذِي الْوَسْوَاسِ», i.e. from the evil of the two kinds.
It is also said that it is maʿṭūf to «الْجِنَّةِ».
